key_insight: Random train/test splits in perovskite-ML benchmarks can massively overestimate performance because duplicated recipes leak across the split, so provenance-grouped evaluation is needed to measure real generalization.
engineering_relevance: For data-driven perovskite device design, this protocol helps researchers choose models and compare results on truly unseen materials, publications, and institutions rather than on memorized historical recipes.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits that separate duplicate devices, papers, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models across progressively harder evaluation regimes.
evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another, making random splits a weak test of physical discovery; performance rankings change sharply when moving to unseen institutions and future data.
watch_item: Grouped splits are stricter and more realistic, but they can reduce apparent benchmark scores and require careful provenance curation to avoid misclassification.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
